Microsoft’s final Outlook outage report details testing gaps and safeguards that backfired

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 21, 2026 at 9:31 amNovember 21, 2026 at 9:50 am.
  • The bug behind last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage struck only newer, more powerful servers in a key part of Microsoft’s network.
  • One reason Microsoft didn’t catch it in advance: it was testing on older servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 21, 2026 at 9:31 amNovember 21, 2026 at 9:50 am.

The bug behind last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage struck only newer, more powerful servers in a key part of Microsoft’s network. That’s because it created a kind of traffic jam inside each server, and the more work a machine tried to do at once, the worse the jam got. The newer servers are built to do more at once, so they’re the ones that seized up.

One reason Microsoft didn’t catch it in advance: it was testing on older servers.

“Our testing did not adequately represent the combination of hardware and traffic mix encountered during this incident,” the tech giant acknowledged in its final report, released Friday evening, a week after resolving the outage that crippled Outlook and cut off email for people around the world.

Testing that more closely replicates the company’s production environment is one of 13 next steps in the report — measures the company notes it will take to keep it from happening again. The list is also aimed at reassuring the businesses that rely on Microsoft for email and collaboration, after CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged at the company’s Ignite conference this week that it has work to do on resilience.

Many of the other steps identified in the report go after a bigger problem: during the incident, the safeguards meant to contain the failure spread it around the world instead.

In a recent development, what set it off: As detailed in Microsoft’s preliminary report last weekend, the bug at the center of the outage had been sitting dormant since July, when Microsoft started rolling out the software update that introduced it. For more than three months, it caused no problems.

It has been revealed that the bug affected the servers that make up what Microsoft calls its network gateway, a front door that connects people to Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services. The flaw came from a Windows update used only on those servers. Standard versions of Windows weren’t affected.

Recent findings suggest that so what was the bug? Microsoft’s final report gives a partial answer, saying it came from a change to how the gateway servers handle incoming connections.

Under heavy load, it turned out, the Windows process that sets up those connections bogged down, with tasks stuck waiting on each other until the servers ran out of computing power and memory and stopped responding.

The final report doesn’t say what the July update was meant to fix. But it does lay out three conditions that finally set the bug off. Without the bug, even all three together would have been routine, the report says.

Sources indicate that first, nearly 14% of the gateway’s server capacity was already offline that day for routine software updates. That’s normally not a problem, because Microsoft keeps enough spare capacity to absorb it. But it meant fewer servers were available to carry the load.

That’s a different explanation from the preliminary report, which blamed the missing capacity on an unrelated problem.

Second, all of Microsoft Teams’ traffic landed on those same servers. Teams normally runs through a separate gateway of its own. About 15 hours before the outage, a routing glitch on that Teams gateway in Microsoft’s US East region set off an automatic switch that moved all Teams traffic worldwide onto the servers that handle email.

Industry observers note that third, the U.S. workday got going. Widespread failures began around 8 a.m. Pacific, as traffic in North America climbed toward its daily peak.

In a recent development, how it spread: As servers stopped responding, Microsoft’s systems automatically moved their traffic to healthy servers nearby, which had the same bug and buckled under the extra load. At the low point, more than 80% of the gateway’s servers in North America were unresponsive.

The system then shifted traffic to other regions, spreading the problem further.

“Within about two hours of the broad failures that began in North America, servers in every region were affected globally,” the report indicates.

Industry observers note that the preliminary report had blamed that spread partly on “a separate matter.” The final report doesn’t repeat or explain that phrase. Instead, its findings say the way Microsoft distributes traffic “can cascade failures to other regions.”.

Industry observers note that once the servers went down, getting them back up was its own problem. As servers came back online, they were swamped by pent-up demand and froze again, a pattern engineers call a “thundering herd.” Microsoft says it will ease traffic back onto recovering servers gradually. That fix doesn’t have a date yet.

The fixes: To keep a failure from spreading again, Microsoft notes it will change how its systems shift traffic between regions, so a problem in one part of the world stays there.

In a recent development, it also intends to split up the servers that handle email, so a surge from another service like Teams can’t take them down. And Teams will switch over only in the region that has the problem, not worldwide.

In a recent development, some of the fixes are due by the end of the year, others by the end of March. Several don’t have a date yet.

It has been revealed that microsoft says its first notice to customers went out about 20 minutes after the outage took hold, and it intends to shorten that by the end of the year. No business email was lost, according to the report, though some delayed messages to consumer mailboxes that had been inactive for more than 30 days bounced back to senders.

In a recent development, the report also confirms what Microsoft stated the day after the outage began: it wasn’t hackers, and it wasn’t AI. “This incident was confirmed not to be caused by a cyberattack, and we found no evidence of malicious activity,” it says. “This change was not caused by AI tooling.”.

Recent findings suggest that the latest testing is supposed to be in place by the end of March, according to the final report. This time, the company says, the machines in the lab will actually match the ones running the service in production.

According to recent reports, affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in people’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a upcoming startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
  • It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding.
  • The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a upcoming startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a strategy that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.

The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal indicates the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.

In a recent development, in practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the tech giant reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.

Sources indicate that CEO Raj Aggarwal says contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”.

Supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.

As Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems toward what’s working and away from what isn’t.

Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.

“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really big impact.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chan Park feels like “an eternal nomad.” He has since age 12, when he moved from Korea to the U.S., where he attended middle school in Minnesota, followed by high school in New Jersey, followed by college in New Hampshire. Then he really began to bounce around. Park worked as a trader in New York out of college, embraced the ski-bum life in Utah, then headed to Asia for Uber, where he spent six years, running its expansion team, then managing its entire Southeast Asia business out of Singapore.

Sources indicate that more specifically, he was responsible for eight countries across the region, and 350 people, which didn’t give him a lot of time to organize his home. But he wasn’t overwhelmed by the chaos. Instead, he says that in Singapore, something unusual happened. “There’s this huge culture of landlords furnishing space to attract expats,” explains Park. “The furnishings aren’t super high-end, but they’re well-designed and well put together, and it enabled me to be basically moved in as soon as I put my clothes in the closet.” Suddenly, coming home was a treat — a newly introduced sensation for him. “For the first time, I was proud to host friends for dinners and barbecues and to just open the door and relax.”.

Park knew his U.S. friends could benefit from the same experience, and before long, he was talking with his Dartmouth classmate turned product and industrial designer Christian Talmage about forming their own tech giant. Enter Oliver Space, which provides a lot of what that Singaporean landlord delivered to Park. It furnishes places for busy professionals, making moving into a new home as easy as hanging up their clothes.

According to recent reports, the now year-old service is available in the Bay Area only. And Oliver Space employs just a dozen people so far. But the company has already gained enough traction to attract $6.8 million in seed funding from an interesting array of investors, including Mayfield, Abstract Ventures, investors Jana Messerschmidt and April Underwood, Opendoor founder Eric Wu, and Kevin and Julia Hartz of Eventbrite, among others.

Now, Oliver Space just has to grow as rapidly, or more so, than other furniture-as-service startups to recently attract funding.

Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January.
  • Sources indicate that the tech giant invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.
  • But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

Sources indicate that the tech giant invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it highlights how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

According to recent reports, nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.”  Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic and OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a big financier of the data center build-out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

According to recent reports, the firm made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earnings call, Kress remarked Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”.

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the organization will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

In a recent development, huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with fresh investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

According to recent reports, “We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress said on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

This week on the GeekWire Podcast, longtime Microsoft beat reporter Mary Jo Foley, a GeekWire contributing writer, sizes up where the company stands after one of its most eventful weeks in years.

Microsoft opened its Ignite conference with an apology for the global Outlook outage, then took direct aim at OpenAI and Anthropic on price, even though it invests in both and sells their models. We discuss the lasting damage from the outage, why enterprise customers have few places to go even when they’re fed up, and Microsoft’s pitch to make Copilot the “OS for work,” as Anthropic goes public.

Mary Jo also explains how Microsoft changed the way it rolls out news at its significant conferences, what got lost along the way, and what that indicates about the company after the shakeup of its communications team. Plus, we weigh who from Microsoft could lead Nvidia, and the GeekWire trivia challenge goes back to 1997.

U.S. spot XRP ETFs held $1.08 billion in total assets as of Nov. 17, according to SoSoValue.

In a recent development, form 13F filings only capture long positions in US-listed securities on a specific date. They don't show shorts, derivative hedges, intra-quarter trading or assets held outside the United States.

5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Crunchbase

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that this is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar.
  • What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth?
  • According to recent reports, those are two of the more unusual ideas that attracted startup investment in the past month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar. Check out our previous entry here.

What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car?

According to recent reports, those are two of the more unusual ideas that attracted startup investment in the past month. Our latest roundup also includes a organization bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a major business. Let’s take a closer look.

Solar power has one rather obvious limitation: The sun goes down.

To that end, Reflect Orbital is working on a solution that sounds straight out of science fiction. The Hawthorne, California-based startup wants to put giant mirrors in orbit to redirect sunlight toward specific locations on Earth, potentially allowing solar farms to keep generating electricity longer after sunset.

Recent findings suggest that the organization recently announced $73.5 million in latest funding, bringing its total funding to more than $102 million, per Crunchbase. Existing investors Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital and Starship Ventures participated, alongside new backers including Buckley Ventures, Convective Capital, The Uncommon Group and Salesforce Ventures 1.

Sources indicate that reflect Orbital is developing lightweight, foldable reflectors that it states can be released aboard satellites and deployed in low Earth orbit. The company envisions using them not only to extend solar power generation, but also to illuminate disaster zones for nighttime search-and-rescue operations or construction sites after dark.

It has been revealed that the idea remains unproven in orbit, however. Reflect Orbital is targeting the second quarter of 2027 for its first demonstration mission, which has received FCC approval. The funding will help support those initial rolls out, further development of its reflector technology, and commercial partnerships.

In a recent development, the raise comes during a record year for space technology funding. By late August, investors had poured $20.3 billion into space- and satellite-related startups globally, per Crunchbase data, already comfortably exceeding previous annual records.

Nasal strips have been around for decades, but Intake Breathing Technology thinks there’s room for a serious upgrade.

The Santa Barbara, California-based consumer wellness company recently announced a $62 million investment from Camino Partners, the investment platform founded by KIND Snacks entrepreneur Daniel Lubetzky.

In a recent development, intake makes a patented magnetic nasal dilator designed to open nasal passages and improve airflow. Rather than relying on a conventional adhesive strip stretched across the nose, its system uses adhesive tabs and a reusable magnetic band to pull the sides of the nose outward.

The company markets its product to people looking to breathe more comfortably while sleeping, exercising or going about their daily routines. It states it has sold more than 100 million pairs of breathing tabs since 2023, with triple-digit revenue growth over the past three years.

Intake plans to use the new capital to expand beyond its direct-to-consumer business and into more mainstream retail channels. That’s where Lubetzky’s experience building KIND into a household name could prove useful.

Sources indicate that its funding comes as venture investors show renewed enthusiasm for fitness and wellness. Startups in those categories raised more than $3.6 billion globally in the first half of 2026, putting the sector on pace for its strongest funding year since 2022, Crunchbase data shows.

Interestingly, much of this year’s investment into the sector has flowed to wearable devices and health platforms built around AI and data. Intake is a somewhat different bet: a relatively simple physical product that has apparently found a sizable audience without promising to reinvent healthcare through software.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Fitness- And Wellness-Related Startup Funding In 2026.

In a recent development, taking out the trash isn’t exactly rocket science. But managing the businesses that collect it turns out to be surprisingly complicated.

San Francisco-based TrashLab Software recently raised $12 million in a growth funding round led by Ventana, with participation from existing investors Bienville Capital, Harlem Capital and CreativeCo.

The startup builds an AI-powered operating platform for waste-hauling businesses, an industry where many smaller operators still rely on spreadsheets, paper routes and clunky software to manage their fleets.

According to recent reports, trashLab says its platform combines dispatching, route planning, customer management, billing and payments. Its AI agent, called Haul-E, can answer customer calls and take orders, while cameras in garbage trucks can help document problems such as overflowing dumpsters, blocked containers or bins that weren’t put out for collection.

The company says hundreds of waste haulers across the U.S. and Canada now use its software, and that more than 5 million tons of material have been managed through its platform.

It’s not the only startup finding an AI opportunity in the waste industry. We recently covered Greyparrot, a London-based organization using computer vision to identify and analyze waste moving through recycling facilities. While Greyparrot focuses on what happens after trash reaches a processing plant, TrashLab is tackling the messy logistics of getting it there.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Venture Funding To Waste Management Startups In 2026.

Factory automation has come a long way, but programming the machines that run industrial production lines can still require specialized expertise and a lot of time.

Gardena, California-based Neuron Industries wants to make the process a lot simpler.

The startup recently announced a $10 million seed round co-led by FCVC and Obvious Ventures, with participation from Y Combinator, Thin Line Capital, Zee Prime Capital and Founder Factor.

Neuron is developing a latest kind of industrial controller — the hardware that coordinates sensors, motors and other equipment in factories — alongside AI-powered software that lets engineers describe what they want a machine to do in ordinary language.

According to recent reports, its system generates control code that engineers can inspect, modify and test in simulation before deploying it to real equipment. The goal is to reduce the time and specialized programming knowledge needed to get newly introduced production lines up and running.

The startup indicates it has already demonstrated its technology on existing factory equipment, including replacing an aging controller on a wood-processing line with roughly three hours of engineering work and eight hours of downtime. It plans to release its Cortex AI Controller commercially in early 2027.

The investment fits into a broader surge in funding for physical AI — technology that applies artificial intelligence to robots, autonomous vehicles, industrial equipment and other machines in the real world. Startups in those categories raised $47.4 billion globally across 521 deals in the first half of 2026, nearly 4x the amount invested in the second half of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Physical AI Venture Funding In 2026.

Sending an experiment into space has traditionally required years of preparation, specialized engineering expertise and a very substantial budget.

Austria-based Tumbleweed wants to bring the cost of entry down to as little as 15,000 euros.

Industry observers note that the Vienna startup recently raised 6.9 million euros (roughly $8 million) in seed funding led by PactVC, with participation from Vanagon Ventures, Prototype Capital and EWOR, among other investors. The organization describes it as the largest space-tech seed round raised in Austria to date.

Tumbleweed develops standardized containers, called Pods, that allow researchers and companies to conduct experiments in microgravity without building their own satellites or navigating the complex certification process required for space missions.

Customers can place their experiments inside the pre-certified containers, which provide power and communications capabilities while in orbit. The startup handles the logistics of launching the payloads and transmitting experimental data back to Earth.

Sources indicate that unlike many space startups still working toward their first launch, Tumbleweed has already put hardware in orbit. Its inaugural Oasis Alpha satellite introduced in July carrying experiments for four paying customers, including research into biological processes and space-resource technologies. The mission was fully booked a year before launch.

Tumbleweed says its upcoming funding will help it carry out three more missions in 2027 and develop a next-generation spacecraft that would allow customers to bring physical samples back to Earth beginning in 2028.

Tumbleweed is part of a growing European space startup ecosystem, although funding remains concentrated elsewhere. As of late August, European companies had attracted about 10% of global space-tech venture investment in 2026, compared with the more than 60% going to U.S. startups, Crunchbase data indicates.

Related Crunchbase query: Space And Satellite Tech Startup Funding.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are presently trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data showed Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S. AI and robotics companies build models that can operate in physical environments.

Recent findings suggest that the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also includes $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Sources indicate that companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult. Startups, including Mecka AI, XDOF, and MicroAGI, are already tackling the problem by collecting real-world data for robotics training. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs aims to compete with them.

Recent findings suggest that humyn Labs has developed its own two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks. It then uses its software to process and label the footage, which means tagging what happens in each clip so AI can learn from it. The startup collects data across over 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India, and South Korea serving as its main hubs, co-founder Manish Agarwal (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

Sources indicate that agarwal, the former CEO of Indian gaming company Nazara Technologies, founded Humyn Labs in February with Ishank Gupta (pictured above, left), a former executive at the brewing giant AB InBev. The duo previously founded Kratos Studios, now known as KGeN. KGeN has a network of contributors across emerging markets, and that network helps Humyn Labs collect data in people’s homes, the founders told TechCrunch.

Collecting footage of human activity is only part of the challenge, Agarwal said. He added that Humyn Labs also uses software to track hand movements, interactions with objects, and other details, turning raw recordings into data that AI models can learn from.

“Scale, diversity, and quality are key aspects, and they need to work in tandem,” Agarwal remarked.

Humyn Labs states it has 12 paying customers, including frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and developers of world models. About 90% of its revenue comes from the U.S., Gupta mentioned, though he declined to name specific customers.

The startup generated $10 million in revenue between April and October and has another $20 million in signed contracts, Agarwal told TechCrunch, adding that a further $20 million in deals has yet to be finalized.

That growth has also increased Humyn Labs’ need for working capital, Agarwal noted, explaining the $21 million venture debt component. The startup pays workers and data collection partners daily or weekly but typically waits 30 to 60 days to receive payments from its AI lab customers. Borrowing helps bridge that gap and is less dilutive than selling more equity, he said.

Over the last few months, India has emerged as a hub for collecting training data for so-called physical AI, with startups, including Human Archive and BuildAI, tapping into the country’s large workforce to record people performing everyday tasks. However, the practice has also raised questions about privacy and consent, particularly when people are recorded inside their homes.

Agarwal mentioned Humyn Labs collects data from people doing their usual work or household chores instead of asking them to perform staged activities. The startup works with local partners to identify collection sites and oversee the process. “The worker is a worker who is incentivized, but he needs to be monitored and supervised for the right input,” he stated.

Humyn Labs at the moment has 51 full-time employees, most based in Bengaluru, plus a network of local partners across the countries where it collects data, Agarwal mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Album VC, a Lehi, Utah-based early-stage venture firm that’s been known until now as Peak Ventures, just gathered up $75 million in capital commitments for its third early-stage fund.

The development highlights investor confidence in Album’s young team, which came together in 2014 after the founder of Zinch — a site connecting colleges and students that sold to the ed-tech tech giant Chegg in 2011 — decided to try his hand at investing in other startups.

As that founder, Sid Krommenhoek — who stayed on with Chegg for several years, running its international efforts — explains it, “I thought I’d do another startup. But I also knew from our own experience in struggling to raise money the need for more capital in Utah, and I thought having that operator-entrepreneur perspective could be useful.”.

In a recent development, A first fund, like many in the industry, was more of an experiment, though it was a decent $23 million, thanks largely to the support of Chegg CEO Dan Rosensweig, who was early to commit capital to the fund. A second ($56 million) fund followed when Krommenhoek and John Mayfield — a friend who joined him from a marketing role at Qualtrics — began investing more seriously in their backyard and beyond.

Industry observers note that they were soon joined by a third investor, Diogo Myrrha, who began as a principal with the firm and is now a general partner. Explains Krommenhoek of one of the many things that binds the three Brigham Young University grads, “We all came into Utah’s orbit when it wasn’t necessarily a place where you could live out your career, but that’s changed.”.

Retail Touchpoints has more here.

Industry observers note that tmunity Therapeutics, a four-year-old, Philadelphia, Pa.-based biotherapeutics company trying to propel a series of cancer-fighting cellular therapies through clinical trials, has raised $75 million in Series B funding led by Andreessen Horowitz. Other investors in the round include Kleiner Perkins, Westlake Village BioPartners, Gilead Sciences, The University of Pennsylvania, Be The Match BioTherapies and BrightEdge Venture Fund. More here and here.

Vindex, a months-old, New York-based esports infrastructure platform founded by a former Activision Blizzard vice president, has raised $60 million in Series A funding from unnamed investors. ESPN has more here.

In a recent development, crunchbase, a 12-year-old, Bay Area-based private tech giant information database that spun out of TechCrunch in 2015, has raised $30 million in Series C funding led by OMERS Ventures. At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

Industry observers note that the Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

It has been revealed that after Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

Recent findings suggest that “So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more rapidly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

Industry observers note that “Several key Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

Tech Report: Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge.
  • According to recent reports, silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures.
  • Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge. Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology.

According to recent reports, silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated.

Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately. But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work.

Recent findings suggest that unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts, and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also reveals where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value.

“The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” remarked Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced. There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.”.

Recent findings suggest that mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology.

Unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch. One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he said, without naming either customer. Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents.

Recent findings suggest that the San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors.

Industry observers note that mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents. The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most vital parts of a document.

“In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra mentioned. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.”.

Sources indicate that the technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts. Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts.

Recent findings suggest that supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer. Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup. The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool. The results have, however, not been independently verified.

Unsiloed also claims to have outperformed competing AI document-processing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark developed by Allen AI. In tests conducted by the startup, Unsiloed scored 88.0, compared with 66.0 for Reducto’s agentic system and 39.9 for Unstructured. The benchmark covered 1,403 PDF pages and tested how well the systems handled tables, mathematical expressions, scanned documents, and complex layouts.

Sources indicate that unsiloed’s pricing, Mishra said, starts at one cent per page. He asserted that the startup’s approach also helps keep its costs down by directing computing power toward the parts of a document that need the most attention, instead of processing every section in the same way.

At the moment, Unsiloed has a headcount of seven people. The startup, Mishra stated, aims to use the fresh funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand its sales efforts, and develop proprietary datasets to improve its technology.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BWA has proposed five major crypto tax and regulatory changes ahead of Budget 2027.
  • The group wants India to reduce the 1% TDS imposed on eligible crypto transactions.
  • BWA wants offshore exchanges serving Indian owners to follow Indian tax and reporting rules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BWA has proposed five major crypto tax and regulatory changes ahead of Budget 2027.

The group wants India to reduce the 1% TDS imposed on eligible crypto transactions.

BWA wants offshore exchanges serving Indian owners to follow Indian tax and reporting rules.

India’s crypto industry is asking the government for a major tax reset ahead of the Union Budget 2027. The Bharat Web3 Association (BWA) has submitted five key recommendations to the Finance Ministry, including a lower 1% TDS, loss relief, and changes to the 30% tax on crypto gains.

It has been revealed that the Bharat Web3 Association shared its recommendations with the Finance Ministry ahead of the Budget. It stated India needs a tax system that encourages people to trade on Indian platforms instead of moving their activity to offshore exchanges.

The demand comes as India’s current VDA tax structure continues to impose a 30% flat tax on gains, along with a 1% TDS on eligible transfers.

Industry observers note that under the Income Tax Act, 2025, traders can deduct only the cost of buying crypto from their taxable gains. They cannot use crypto losses to reduce other gains or carry those losses forward.

This makes the 1% TDS a major concern for active traders.

Therefore, BWA believes the current framework needs to be reviewed to make compliance more practical while keeping the government’s tax and reporting controls in place.

However, BWA has proposed five major changes to India’s crypto tax and regulatory framework.

The impact of India’s current crypto tax structure can also be seen in where users are trading.

According to a TIOL Knowledge Foundation report, around 95% of India’s crypto trading volume moved to offshore exchanges in FY 2025–26, while only 5.4% took place on Indian platforms.

The report estimates that India has around 30 million active crypto people, with roughly 3 million to 5 million users moving to offshore platforms after the government introduced the 1% TDS on crypto transactions.

Recent findings suggest that the shift has also appeared in user activity. Between July 2025 and April 2026, visits by Indian consumers to a major offshore peer-to-peer platform increased 73%, while purchases grew 3.6 times.

It has been revealed that this migration could also have a major impact on government tax collections. The report estimates that the government may have missed around ₹19,049 crore ($2 billion) in TDS and ₹57,147 crore ($6.18 billion) in capital gains tax through FY 2025–26 as trading activity moved to offshore platforms.

The numbers explain why the offshore-exchange matter has become a central part of BWA’s recommendations.

BWA believes the current framework needs to be reviewed to make compliance more practical while keeping the government’s tax and reporting controls in place.

The association claims these changes could encourage more users to participate through compliant Indian platforms rather than shifting activity elsewhere.

The proposals go beyond changing taxes for domestic users.

Recent findings suggest that BWA wants Indian tax and TDS requirements to apply more clearly to offshore crypto exchanges serving Indian users. The association argues that Indian platforms face significant compliance obligations while offshore competitors can attract the same users without facing an equivalent regulatory burden.

It has also called for stronger enforcement of registration and reporting requirements for offshore entities operating in the Indian market.

Another major matter is access to global liquidity.

In a recent development, BWA wants clear rules for FIU-IND-registered Indian VDA platforms that access liquidity through offshore exchanges. It has called for clearer guidance under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), particularly where different interpretations have created uncertainty for compliant platforms.

Sources indicate that the broader regulatory framework is also becoming more demanding. Reporting entities face penalties for delayed or inaccurate transaction statements, while cross-border crypto-asset reporting under the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) is scheduled to begin in April 2027.

The industry’s argument is becoming harder to separate from the numbers: India has a 30% tax on VDA gains, a 1% TDS and restrictions on using crypto losses, while reporting and compliance requirements are also expanding.

These rules were left unchanged in the 2026–27 Union Budget. BWA is now asking the Finance Ministry to reconsider the framework before Budget 2027.

Its five main demands are clear: reduce the 1% TDS, allow loss set-off and carry-forward, review the 30% tax, strengthen rules for offshore exchanges and clarify FEMA requirements for global liquidity access.

In a recent development, for BWA, the goal is not simply lower taxes. It is to create a system where compliant Indian platforms can compete, customers have clearer rules and the government can strengthen oversight and tax collection without driving more crypto activity offshore.

Budget 2027 will show whether the government is willing to make that shift.

The BWA submission focused on the need for a fair, balanced and effective taxation framework that encourages compliance, strengthens investor protection, enhances tax revenues and supports the growth of India’s domestic Web3 ecosystem.

BWA highlighted several key recommendations, including:.

Industry observers note that 1. Ensuring a level playing field: Clarifying and strengthening the applicability of Indian tax provisions, particularly TDS obligations, to offshore VDA platforms serving Indian users, so that compliant domestic platforms are not placed at a competitive disadvantage.

In a recent development, 2. Rationalising VDA taxation: Reconsidering the existing 1% TDS, permitting the set-off and carry-forward of losses, and reviewing the 30% tax rate to encourage greater participation through compliant Indian platforms.

3. Strengthening compliance and accountability: Improving the enforcement of registration and reporting obligations and ensuring that offshore entities serving Indian owners are subject to appropriate Indian legal and regulatory requirements.

We also drew attention to the need for regulatory clarity regarding access to global liquidity by FIU-IND-registered Indian VDA platforms through offshore exchanges, particularly in the context of ongoing enquiries and differing interpretations under FEMA.

Clear and consistent guidelines, developed in consultation with the relevant authorities, would provide much-needed certainty to compliant Indian platforms, strengthen the domestic ecosystem and help ensure that Indian consumers continue to access transparent, accountable and compliant channels.

BWA’s central message was that effective taxation, regulatory certainty and a level playing field can reinforce one another.

A framework that encourages activity within compliant Indian platforms can strengthen oversight, improve tax compliance and support innovation and investment in India.

BWA remains committed to working constructively with the Government and regulatory authorities towards a responsible, transparent and globally competitive VDA ecosystem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated plans to launch two new XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

Recent findings suggest that as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn plans to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

Sources indicate that interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its plans to launch these two ETFs.

It has been revealed that roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

Sources indicate that unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

According to recent reports, A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

It has been revealed that notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

Recent findings suggest that U.K.-based fintech Payhawk announced a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the company at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.

In a recent development, founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, stated the firm saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”.

According to recent reports, payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and says it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the company noted it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

In a recent development, ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

Paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

It has been revealed that about $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

Recent findings suggest that ripple launched RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

According to recent reports, RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the Latest York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he remarked.

Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous firm to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

Industry observers note that the B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Substantial Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.

“We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”.

Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song stated, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

According to recent reports, because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song mentioned the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical challenges since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she noted. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”.

According to recent reports, everful prepares to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.

The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

Solana has remained one of the major cryptocurrencies that have been heavily affected by the persistent crypto market volatility, stalling demand from both retail and institutional investors.

While Solana has continued to struggle amid the growing market uncertainty, it appears that traders are increasingly exiting their positions even across its DeFi market.

Recent data showcased by blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain shows that two Solana whales unstaked a total of 2.31 million SOL on November 19.

While the total amount of SOL unstaked was worth about $169.4 million, further data highlighted that the whales proceeded to transfer the tokens to Coinbase, a leading cryptocurrency exchange in the U.S.

It is important to note that the act of withdrawing SOL previously committed to the network's staking mechanism is regarded as unstaking.

While this move automatically gives holders the ability to transfer, sell, or use the unstaked tokens, the massive unstaking of 2.31 million SOL from large holders has drawn attention within the crypto community regarding the intention behind the move.

With curiosity on the rise about the whales' decision to move such a large amount of SOL to Coinbase Prime, the timing of the move has triggered speculation that the whales may be intending to sell the tokens.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.

Leading cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has unveiled the official listing of artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic (ANT) shares on its trading platform in the U.S. and U.K.

Recent findings suggest that the listing comes as Anthropic, the company behind the popular AI chatbot Claude, officially made its much-anticipated stock market debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, with its shares seeing massive volatility.

It has been revealed that as per the latest X post from Coinbase, the exchange confirmed the availability of Anthropic (ANT) shares for eligible customers in the U.S. and U.K.

According to recent reports, it's crucial to mention that ANT isn't a cryptocurrency but a traditional stock. Coinbase's support for ANT shares shows the company's efforts to expand its offerings beyond crypto into traditional financial markets.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic has set a new historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

The artificial intelligence organization sold 980 million shares at $83 per share, significantly higher than its previously declared price range of $70 to $78.

This brought Anthropic's initial valuation to about $1.5 trillion, making the manufacturer one of the most valuable publicly listed firms in the world right from the get-go.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

As per Reuters, Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50. This represented an enormous 34% premium over the IPO price.

At the initial peak, Anthropic's market cap exceeded $2 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's valuation when it debuted on the market in June.

Anthropic shares slipped to around $95 as the stock gave back a significant chunk of its gains. This was partly due to investors looking to book their profits.

Nonetheless, Anthropic shares were still trading comfortably above their $83 IPO price.

The volatility surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut signals increasing doubts about the AI investment craze.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

Instead of just providing cryptocurrency trading, the exchange is looking to become a platform for multiple asset classes.

Interestingly, Coinbase had already listed Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures for eligible non-U.S. users on Nov. 18.

The perpetual futures were derivative contracts that allowed traders to speculate on Anthropic's valuation before its shares officially started trading on Nasdaq.

With the latest listing, eligible Coinbase users in the U.S. and U.K. can now trade the publicly listed Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

The US stock market crash intensified this week as investors aggressively dumped technology and artificial intelligence stocks, pushing major Wall Street indexes toward their steepest weekly declines in years. The Nasdaq Composite plunged approximately 10%, marking its worst week since the March 2020 pandemic crash, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6%.

Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones entered correction territory, raising concerns that the AI-driven market rally may be facing a deeper repricing.

With technology stocks leading the decline, investors are now questioning whether the latest stock market crash signals a temporary correction or the beginning of a broader downturn.

Wall Street’s losses accelerated on Friday, with major indexes closing sharply lower after another wave of selling hit AI and semiconductor stocks.

On Friday, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to close at 6,910.39, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% to 22,617.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 949 points, closing at 48,147.33.

The S&P 500 and Dow are now more than 10% below their recent record highs, confirming corrections in both indexes. The Nasdaq has also erased its gains for 2026.

The latest stock market crash is primarily driven by growing concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence trade. Investors have poured enormous capital into AI infrastructure, chipmakers and data-center companies.

However, rising valuations and uncertainty over whether AI investments can generate sufficient returns are prompting investors to reassess the sector’s growth expectations. The sell-off intensified following the market’s reaction to Anthropic’s public debut, which failed to restore confidence in AI stocks. Investors also remain concerned about interest rates, inflation and the possibility of tighter monetary conditions.

The result has been a sharp unwinding of crowded technology trades, with losses spreading beyond individual AI companies into the broader stock market.

In a recent development, semiconductor stocks have suffered the most severe losses as investors reduce exposure to AI-related companies. Nvidia fell approximately 23% for the week, marking its worst weekly performance since 2008. AMD lost around 20.5%, while Micron and other chipmakers also faced significant selling pressure.

Industry observers note that the semiconductor sector’s 17.1% weekly decline highlights the scale of the repricing underway in the AI trade. Companies that previously drove Wall Street’s rally are now becoming the biggest contributors to the market’s losses.

The immediate outlook for Wall Street remains uncertain. The latest correction has raised concerns about valuations, AI spending and investor positioning, but a correction does not automatically signal a prolonged bear market.

Industry observers note that investors will closely watch whether technology stocks stabilize, whether volatility eases and whether companies can deliver earnings growth strong enough to justify their valuations. For now, the stock market crash has exposed the risks of Wall Street’s heavy dependence on AI stocks.

If selling continues across semiconductor and technology companies, the broader market could remain under pressure heading into the next trading week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainflip lost nearly $4.86 million after an attacker drained its Ethereum vault.

he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.

The latest incident marks Chainflip’s second major security breach in just over two months.

Chainflip, a decentralized cross-chain swap protocol, has faced another security scare after nearly $4.86 million in crypto was drained from its Ethereum vault in a single transaction. The attacker moved the stolen funds through Tornado Cash within just nine minutes, forcing the protocol to halt deposits, withdrawals, and swaps.

While its team investigates how the funds were taken.

On-chain investigations by Bitquery show that the attacker targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic key system rather than exploiting a bug in its smart contracts.

The attacker first obtained a valid Schnorr signature from the Ethereum Vault’s Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) aggregate key. This allowed the attacker to pass the vault’s normal signature checks.

It has been revealed that on November 21, 2026, a newly funded wallet (0x78fa) called the Vault.transferBatch function. The transaction passed verification and drained all the vault’s available funds in a single move.

The attacker then moved rapidly to hide the stolen funds. Within nine minutes, the exploiter swapped the 3,249,631.41 USDC and 758,141.33 USDT for 2,909 ETH (worth around $4.86 million), then sent it to Tornado Cash in 38 separate batches.

It has been revealed that chainflip has not yet confirmed the $4.86 million loss. Instead, the protocol noted it was aware of a potential exploit affecting its vaults and moved into full safe mode as a precaution.

Sources indicate that we’re aware of a potential exploit affecting Chainflip vaults.As a precaution, the protocol is being put into full safe mode. Deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quoting are disabled.We’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.

“Deposits, withdrawals, swaps, and quoting are disabled; we’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.”.

Sources indicate that this is Chainflip’s second major attack in just over two months. On September 12, 2026, the protocol lost $736,442 in a separate exploit targeting its TRON integration. That attack was caused by a software flaw in how Chainflip processed TRON transaction data, while the November 21 attack targeted its Ethereum Vault’s cryptographic signing key.

After the September attack, Chainflip paused TRON swaps and used its surplus reserves to fully reimburse affected liquidity providers in USDC.

The protocol has yet to confirm whether it will follow the same recovery strategy for the latest $4.86 million loss.

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the manufacturer.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it launched its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data highlights that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

According to recent reports, three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data demonstrates that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain.".

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Industry observers note that through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan notes on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

It has been revealed that on 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Recent findings suggest that some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

Sources indicate that $2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is noted to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

Sources indicate that according to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

Industry observers note that however, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

Industry observers note that for the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

"I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".
